findings.summary: assert conflict["expected_version"] == 0 compares the response field against the literal the test itself passed in, so the two sides move together and it cannot fail on a regression; it is not an independent guard, though no score rests on it because the four new capabilities are each guarded by an independent assertion.
findings.text: tests/test_a_refused_write_names_the_next_step.py:150 compares conflict["expected_version"] to 0, the value the test itself supplied to _edit, so it holds whatever the code echoes and survives a regression; the new capabilities are each guarded independently (changed_targets against fixture value 1.0, refused_ops indices, replay new_version tied to file version).

findings.summary: _value_at_path re-inlines the by-id list lookup the store already owns at reckon/_store.py:2396 (_find_by_id) and mirrors a subset of _apply_set's accepted path forms without extending that owner, so the two resolutions must be kept in sync by hand.
findings.text: reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:955 finds a list element with next((item for item in listed if str(item.get("id")) == parts[1])) instead of reusing reckon/_store.py:2396 _find_by_id, the store's owned by-id lookup, so the new reader duplicates a capability the repository owns.

findings.summary: the PROJECT_RESOURCE_TYPES branch returns version conflicts unwrapped (no changed_targets) and never records or replays a request_id, so the goal's "each edit_plan refusal" holds only for plan-path writes.
findings.text: reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:1233 handles doc_types in PROJECT_RESOURCE_TYPES and its ProjectStateConflict return calls _conflict_response without _attach_changed_targets, and never reaches record_write_receipt, so a resource write's conflict names no changed targets and its request_id retry is not idempotent.
